payload.message:
JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Carina, Clarinda, Ivette, Shonna

payload.content:
Hello team, this is Ivette. I am available for 4 hours and have strong skills in infrastructure and documentation. I am considering the following tasks based on priority and cost: 
- ISSUE-0001::triage (cost=2.96, medium priority)
- ISSUE-0002::review (cost=3.16, critical priority)
- ISSUE-0001::review (cost=3.70, medium priority)
- ISSUE-0001::docs (cost=3.70, medium priority)
I would like to know if anyone else is targeting these tasks or any preference for coordination to avoid duplicates.

Ivette here again. Just to add, I am leaning towards claiming ISSUE-0002::review due to its critical priority and reasonable cost. Please let me know if someone else is planning to take it or if it fits well with your plans. Open to suggestions for optimal task distribution.

Clarinda here. I have 9 hours available and strong skills in infrastructure. I am evaluating tasks with medium priority related to infrastructure such as ISSUE-0001::implement, review, test, docs, and triage. Ivette, I see you lean towards ISSUE-0002::review, which seems a good critical priority task. I want to avoid duplication and coordinate on task choices.

Clarinda proposes to take ISSUE-0001::triage (medium priority, cost=2.94) to complement Ivette's likely take on ISSUE-0002::review. This would maximize task coverage with minimal overlap. Please confirm if you have other preferences or conflicts.

Carina here. I have 8 hours available and strong skills in documentation. I am considering the critical priority tasks in ISSUE-0002 related to documentation, especially review or test, as they align with my skills and availability. Ivette, I see you lean towards ISSUE-0002::review. If you are confident in taking that, I might consider ISSUE-0002::test or skip if needed. Clarinda, your choice of ISSUE-0001::triage looks good to me to avoid overlap.

Hello team, Shonna here. I have 7 hours available and my top skill is machine-learning. I see Ivette is leaning towards ISSUE-0002::review and Clarinda is considering ISSUE-0001::triage. Given my strong machine-learning skill, I am interested in ISSUE-0001::implement, but I want to confirm if anyone else plans to take it or if it fits well with the team's distribution. I want to avoid duplicates and help maximize task coverage.
Shonna checking in. I prefer to pick ISSUE-0001::implement due to my strong machine-learning skills and manageable cost, but open to feedback if others have strong preferences for this task.

Shonna here again. Just to add, if ISSUE-0001::implement is taken by someone else, I can consider ISSUE-0001::triage as an alternative, although it's less ideal due to higher cost for me. Looking forward to team input to finalize choices.

Ivette here. I appreciate everyone's updates and coordination. I agree with Clarinda taking ISSUE-0001::triage and Shonna targeting ISSUE-0001::implement given her machine-learning strength. I will plan to take ISSUE-0002::review (critical priority) as it's a good match for my documentation skill and reasonable cost. Carina, your plan for ISSUE-0002::test sounds good to me. Let's confirm these choices to maximize coverage and minimize overlap. Open to any feedback or adjustments. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Clarinda here. Confirming my plan to take ISSUE-0001::triage (medium priority, cost=2.94) to complement Ivette's likely claim on ISSUE-0002::review. This coordination should maximize task coverage and avoid duplication. Open to feedback or adjustments.

Carina here. I agree with Ivette taking ISSUE-0002::review to leverage her documentation skill and reasonable cost. I plan to take ISSUE-0002::test, which aligns with my skills and availability, to complement the team's choices and maximize task coverage. Clarinda's plan for ISSUE-0001::triage and Shonna's for ISSUE-0001::implement look well coordinated. Looking forward to finalizing this distribution.

Shonna here. I confirm my preference for ISSUE-0001::implement due to my strong machine-learning skills and manageable cost. I support Ivette's plan for ISSUE-0002::review, Clarinda's for ISSUE-0001::triage, and Carina's for ISSUE-0002::test. This distribution seems optimal for maximizing task coverage and minimizing overlap. Looking forward to final confirmation from everyone.
